nodes.label: Job owner
nodes.summary: Registers periodic jobs or schedules one-off tasks, and monitors their runs.

nodes.label: Cron service
nodes.summary: A few replicas (three by default) sharing state through Paxos; spread across power domains in one datacenter (Google).

nodes.label: Cron leader
nodes.summary: The only replica that changes state or launches jobs. Records the start of a launch through Paxos before launching and its end after; stops talking to the datacenter scheduler as soon as it loses leadership.

nodes.label: Follower replicas
nodes.summary: Track every job's next launch time and all open launches, so one can take over within the one-minute failover target.

nodes.label: Paxos log and snapshots
nodes.summary: Logs and snapshots on each replica's local disk; snapshots also backed up to the distributed filesystem; logs are not.

nodes.label: Datacenter scheduler
nodes.summary: Runs the launched jobs on machines (Borg at Google). Job names include the scheduled launch time, so a new leader can look up whether a launch happened.

nodes.label: Task frontend
nodes.summary: Accepts Schedule RPCs for immediate or delayed tasks and writes them to the task store (Dropbox ATF).

nodes.label: Task store
nodes.summary: Holds task state and payload, indexed by the next trigger timestamp; every state change also moves that timestamp so stalled tasks are polled again.

nodes.label: Store Consumer
nodes.summary: Polls the store (every two seconds at the time) for due and retrying tasks and pushes them onto the right queue.

nodes.label: Per-type priority queues
nodes.summary: One SQS queue per (lambda, priority) pair, buffering between the poller and the workers and isolating task types.

nodes.label: Worker hosts
nodes.summary: Each host runs one Controller that pulls from queues and serves tasks, and Executors that run the callback, heartbeat, and stop themselves after three failed heartbeats.

nodes.label: Heartbeat and Status Controller
nodes.summary: Serves ClaimTask, Heartbeat and SetResults; a task can be claimed only from the Enqueued state, which prevents concurrent execution.

nodes.label: Dead letter queue
nodes.summary: Proposed by Dropbox for tasks stuck in retry loops: cap retries, park the task, reschedule after the fix. A proposal in the post, not a described component.

edges.label: launch start / end via Paxos quorum
launch job named by scheduled time
new leader: look up open launches

steps.caption: The owner registers a job; the schedule may use ? so the system picks a start minute by hashing.
At the scheduled time the leader records the launch start in Paxos and waits for the quorum.
Only then it asks the datacenter scheduler to run the job, named with its scheduled time.
The leader records the launch end; followers update the next launch time.
State changes go to the log; periodic snapshots bound its size.
A client schedules a task for a future time.
The task is stored with its next trigger timestamp.
When it is due, the Store Consumer's poll picks it up.
It is pushed onto the queue for its type and priority.
A Controller pulls it for an Executor.
The task is claimed, heartbeats while running, and reports its result.
The store records the final state; retriable failures get a new trigger time.
The start of the launch is recorded but no end arrives; the launch is open.
A follower becomes leader within seconds and looks up the precomputed job name, which includes the scheduled time.
It launches only if the job is missing; if lookup were impossible, the policy prefers skipping over a double launch.
Three heartbeats in a row fail; the Executor terminates itself.
After the longer heartbeat timeout the task's trigger time has passed, so the poller finds it again.
It is re-enqueued and claimed by another worker, with no overlap with the dead one.
The handler keeps returning a retriable failure and the task is rescheduled again and again.
With a retry cap, it moves to a dead letter queue instead of eating scheduling capacity (Dropbox's proposal).
